text.name: helpLine_cs_p1_intro_text
text.text: [EN] Seasonal Crop Stress gives every field its own soil moisture, from 0% (bone dry) to 100% (saturated). Rain fills it, heat and time dry it, and irrigation lets you put water back. While a crop is in its thirsty growth window and the field is drier than that crop needs, drought stress builds, and at harvest that stress takes a share of the yield. The Esc page lists the fields you own.

text.name: helpLine_cs_p1_start_text
text.text: [EN] Open the moisture HUD with the Controls action Toggle Moisture HUD (factory Right Shift+M; if nothing happens, look under Options > Controls > Seasonal Crop Stress, it may be bound to another key). Green fields are fine, yellow need water soon, red are losing yield. The Esc menu page Realistic Farming > Crop Stress lists your fields with moisture, stress and irrigation; click a row for the detail card. Build a Water Pump first, then a Center Pivot within 500 m of it.

text.name: helpLine_cs_p2_how_text
text.text: [EN] Every in-game hour each field loses about 0.4% moisture before modifiers. Hot weather and summer speed that up, cool weather and winter slow it down. Rain and a sprayer filled with water add moisture. The Difficulty setting scales drying (Easy 0.7x, Normal 1.0x, Hard 1.4x) and the Evapotranspiration setting scales it again. The ground also holds water unevenly: low spots stay wetter longer and the high, dry patches show first.

text.name: helpLine_cs_p2_soil_text
text.text: [EN] Sandy soil dries 1.4 times faster than loamy and soaks up rain 1.25 times faster, so it swings quickly both ways. Clay dries at 0.7 times and takes rain at 0.72 times, so it holds water longest. Loamy is the 1.0 reference and the easiest to manage. The soil type shows on the HUD row and on the Esc detail card.

text.name: helpLine_cs_p3_window_text
text.text: [EN] Each crop has a thirsty growth window and its own moisture need. Stress builds every hour the crop is in that window and the field sits below that need, and it does not heal when rain returns. Needs at a glance: wheat 35%, barley 30%, corn 40%, canola 45%, sunflower 30%, soybeans 40%, sugar beet 50%, potato 55%, rice 70%. Other crops have their own window and need in the same table.

text.name: helpLine_cs_p3_yield_text
text.text: [EN] At harvest the yield is cut by the field's stress times your Max Yield Loss setting. The factory cap is 30%, so a fully stressed field still yields 70%; the setting can be raised as far as 75%. A new crop after harvest starts clean. The Esc page and the Crop Consultant show the yield risk per field, so water where it matters most.

text.name: helpLine_cs_p5_types_text
text.text: [EN] Two placeables live in the build menu. The Water Pump feeds the pivots and must sit within 500 m of a system; pressure drops about 30% at that full range, so keep pumps close. A Center Pivot waters a circle and comes in three spans. A pivot with no pump in range shows Disconnected. The shop also sells the irrigator vehicles, and a sprayer filled with WATER raises moisture wherever you spray it, handy for a small field or a corner a pivot cannot reach.

text.name: helpLine_cs_p5_schedule_text
text.text: [EN] Open a system's Irrigation Manager with the Controls action Open Irrigation Manager, or with the Schedule chip on the pivot card of the Esc Crop Stress page when that system covers the selected field. Pick the days of the week, set a start and end hour, and Save. Irrigate Now waters the covered fields for one hour straight away. With Irrigation Costs on, a running system is charged per hour. Finite Water is off by default and is an experimental system: it takes effect only when both it and Experimental Systems are on. Then each pump carries a store in irrigation hours that runs consume and rain refills.

text.name: helpLine_cs_p6_what_text
text.text: [EN] The Crop Consultant (Controls action Open Crop Consultant, no factory key) ranks your riskiest fields by moisture and stress, gives a plain recommendation for the next 24 hours and shows the moisture forecast. Healthy is 40% and up, Warning is 25% to 40%, Critical is below 25%.

text.name: helpLine_cs_p6_act_text
text.text: [EN] Critical fields need water today, before yield loss grows. Warning fields should be watered within a day or two, or left to forecast rain if it is close. A field already building stress shows an exclamation mark on the HUD. Use the consultant's Open Irrigation Manager control to schedule the worst field first.

text.name: helpLine_cs_p6_npc_text
text.text: [EN] Other mods plug in when present. NPC Favor: the agronomist's favors unlock early drought warnings and irrigation advice. Soil and Fertilizer: high organic matter holds water, acid soil (pH under 6.0) stresses crops earlier; Crop Stress reads the soil manager through the mission handle. UsedPlus: irrigation running costs and wear. CoursePlay and AutoDrive: vehicle counts and water destinations in the alerts.

text.name: helpLine_cs_s1_gen_text
text.text: [EN] ESC > Settings > Seasonal Crop Stress. Enable Mod switches the whole system on or off without touching your irrigation placeables. Difficulty scales how fast stress builds and how fast fields dry: Easy 0.5x stress and 0.7x drying, Normal 1.0x, Hard 1.5x stress and 1.4x drying.

text.name: helpLine_cs_s1_evap_text
text.text: [EN] Evapotranspiration Rate scales drying on top of difficulty. Slow keeps moisture in the ground and makes rain go further. Fast can dry a field within a game day in hot weather, so scheduled irrigation becomes essential.

text.name: helpLine_cs_s2_yield_text
text.text: [EN] Max Yield Loss caps the share of the harvest that stress can take. The factory value is 30%, so a fully stressed field still yields 70%; it can be raised as far as 75%. Critical Threshold (factory 25%, 15% to 35%) is the moisture level where the red Critical band and its alerts begin; each crop's own need still decides when stress builds.

text.name: helpLine_cs_s2_alerts_text
text.text: [EN] Irrigation Costs charges an hourly fee while a system runs; turn it off for a simpler game. Alerts Enabled shows a warning when a field needs water, and Alert Cooldown (factory 12 hours) is the minimum time before the same field alerts again. Finite Water is off by default and is an experimental system: it takes effect only when both it and Experimental Systems are on. Then each pump carries a store in irrigation hours that scheduled runs and Irrigate Now consume and rain refills.

text.name: helpLine_cs_p4_hud_text
text.text: [EN] The moisture HUD (Controls action Toggle Moisture HUD, factory Right Shift+M) lists every tracked field with crop, growth stage, a colour bar and the moisture percentage, with the forecast strip above it. Edit mode (Controls action Edit/Move Moisture HUD, factory Right Shift+N) lets you drag and resize the panes; the layout is saved per player.

text.name: helpLine_cs_p4_reading_text
text.text: [EN] Each row shows the field number, the crop, its growth stage, the moisture bar and the percentage. An exclamation mark at the end means that field is already building drought stress. Only crops that can suffer drought stress are listed.

text.name: helpLine_cs_p4_status_text
text.text: [EN] Green is Healthy: 40% moisture and up, nothing to do. Yellow is Warning: 25% to 40%, plan water. Red is Critical: below 25%, yield loss can start, water now. The same bands colour the Esc Crop Stress page.

text.name: helpLine_cs_p4_keys_text
text.text: [EN] Toggle Moisture HUD: factory Right Shift+M. Edit/Move Moisture HUD: factory Right Shift+N. Open Irrigation Manager, Open Crop Consultant and Open Crop Stress Settings have no factory key: bind them under Options > Controls > Seasonal Crop Stress. The Esc page Realistic Farming > Crop Stress has a Help footer that opens the two-column guide.

text.name: helpLine_cs_t2_sandy_text
text.text: [EN] Sandy soil dries 1.4 times faster than loamy and twice as fast as clay. If you farm mixed soils, put the first pivot on the sandy fields. A pivot over a large sandy area is often a better buy than one on a small clay field that holds water on its own.

text.name: helpLine_cs_t2_forecast_text
text.text: [EN] The forecast strip shows whether moisture is heading up or down. If rain is a day or two away and the field is only in the yellow band, wait and save the running cost. Act early when several dry days line up with a thirsty growth window, especially on sandy fields.

text.name: helpLine_cs_i1_about_text
text.text: [EN] Created by TisonK. Adds soil moisture per field, crop stress in thirsty growth windows, a harvest cut capped at 30% by default, and irrigation placeables with schedules, all inside Farming Simulator 25. Every field, every season, every decision counts.

text.name: helpLine_cs_i2_npc_text
text.text: [EN] With NPC Favor installed, the agronomist's favors unlock early drought warnings and specialist irrigation advice. With Soil and Fertilizer installed, each field's organic matter and pH change how fast it dries: high organic matter holds water, acid soil below pH 6.0 stresses crops earlier. Crop Stress reads the soil manager through the mission handle, so the two mods load in any order.

text.name: helpLine_cs_i2_vehicle_text
text.text: [EN] With CoursePlay active, the number of vehicles working a stressed field appears in that field's alert. With AutoDrive, critical alerts include water destination counts. With UsedPlus, hourly irrigation running costs and equipment wear are tracked. Multiplayer: the server runs moisture, stress and irrigation and sends the results to every client; the HUD layout is saved per player.

text.name: helpLine_cs_t3_sprayer_text
text.text: [EN] A vehicle sprayer filled with WATER is a manual irrigation tool: every area you spray gets an immediate moisture boost. Use it on small fields, on a corner a pivot does not reach, or as a stopgap until a pump and a pivot are affordable.

text.name: cs_rf_pda_select_field
text.text: Select a field in the table for details.

text.name: rf_pda_side_info_soil
text.text:
[EN] Soil Fertilizer
This table lists every field you own. One row = one field.
Columns: Field #, Area, N/P/K (% of a healthy target), Status (Good / Fair / Poor), Fertilizer need (short cue for what still looks short).
Click a row. Treatment (below) is the plan for that field: - PRODUCT = what to buy (first is preferred; "or ..." is an alternate) - RATE = amount per area / TOTAL = amount for this field - Selected names the field; Next (under it) says what to do first
How to apply: dry goods (urea, MAP, potash, lime) go through a fertilizer spreader; liquids go in a sprayer tank. If pH and nutrients both show, fix lime or gypsum first so nutrients can work. Weed, pest, or disease lines mean spray (or weed mechanically) before you expect a full crop.
Start with the weakest Status, open Treatment, follow Next, then the rest of the list.

text.name: rf_pda_side_info_crop_stress
text.text:
[EN] Crop Stress
This screen is the Crop Stress desk. Each line is one field you own.
The table shows Field, Crop, Moisture, Stress, Irrigated, and Status. Moisture is how wet the soil is. Stress is how hard the crop is fighting dry spells. Irrigated says a system can reach this field. Status is Healthy, Warning, or Critical.
Click a row. Field Detail on the left coaches that field and Next says the first job. AGRONOMIST on the right lists the top risk fields. PIVOT below drives the irrigation system for the selected field.
On PIVOT, grey remotes are locked until the step before them is done. Open the door, then power, then the rest. An empty seat means no pivot covers this field.
Start with Critical Status, follow Next, then work up the list.
Irrigator kit (shop): pump + Rainstar + pull bar. Unfold, pull the gun out, turn it on over a field.
